author: Kai Moreno
title: Model warmup and cold start on Dedicated
content:
# Purpose
Dedicated pools that have been idle can take 30–90 seconds on the first request. This is not a retired model and not an outage.

# When to use
Dedicated pools that have been idle can take 30–90 seconds on the first request. This is not a retired model and not an outage.

# What Support does
If they say the first request after a quiet night is slow and later requests are fine, send the warmup guide. P4, Support. Do not add model-retirement. Do not page for a single cold start.

# Intake
Collect the customer, the project or pool name, the region if they named one, and the outcome they want. Write those on the SUP ticket before you route.

# Priority and routing
If they say the first request after a quiet night is slow and later requests are fine, send the warmup guide. P4, Support. Do not add model-retirement. Do not page for a single cold start. If this page and a more specific SOP both apply, the more specific SOP wins.

# Guardrails
Do not issue credits. Do not disable an org API key from this page. Do not invent a label this page does not name.

# Customer reply
Thanks, we have the request. We will follow the internal playbook for this kind of ticket and update you on the SUP thread.

# Related
Support intake checklist. Severity matrix for anything that is actually down. This page is only for the purpose above.
